value: Study analyzed >6,500 publicly available metagenomes from 36 datasets spanning 6 continents and 25 countries
1,023 P. copri genomes reconstructed: 17 isolate sequences and 1,006 MAGs
72 reference genomes used (15 newly sequenced isolates, 2 public reference isolates, 55 manually curated MAGs)
P. copri complex comprises four genetically distinct clades (A, B, C, D)
Clades show >10% inter-clade ANI distance, well above 5-6% species delineation threshold
Analysis of ancient gut metagenomes from Iceman (5,300 years old) and pre-Columbian coprolites
All four clades nearly ubiquitous and co-present in non-Westernized populations
Multi-generational dietary modifications proposed as driver of reduced P. copri prevalence in Westernized populations
Distinct carbohydrate metabolism repertoires observed between clades
Clade delineation time pre-dates human migration waves out of Africa (~6.5 million years ago for clade B divergence)
No strong evidence of clade association with disease (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) in meta-analysis
Familial transmission of P. copri detected in 19.2% of family pairs analyzed
Recent sequencing of cohorts from Ghana (44 individuals), Ethiopia (50 individuals), Tanzania (68 individuals)
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: cross-continent meta-analysis exploiting >6,500 metagenomes, we obtained >1,000 genomes and explored the genetic and population structure of P. copri
uncurated_metadata.notes: Key study design features, sample sizes, and major findings not captured by structured fields.
